clue.text: Know-how that hurts in the media

indicators.note: in places one thing inside another, so the cry of pain sits within the word for the media

parts.note: the press is the news media
OW is the cry of something that hurts

explanation.surface: A complaint that expertise is being damaged by newspapers and broadcasters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That hurts' is the exclamation of pain itself, not a verb phrase about the media.
explanation.definitionFit: Prowess is skill or expertise at doing something, a close synonym for practical ability.

indicators.note: something that backfires goes the wrong way, so the preceding letters are read backwards

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for right
taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: The whole string R, A, LUGER is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A regular is a professional soldier of a standing army, as opposed to a reservist or volunteer.

clue.text: Jam and a piece of cheese?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to force something tightly into a space
second meaning: a triangular slice cut from a round cheese

explanation.surface: It reads like a snack order of jam with some cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: Jam looks like the fruit preserve, but it is a verb meaning to cram in.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for fixing something firmly in a gap and a noun for a thick triangular portion.

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed above, so the bird comes first

parts.note: a large white water bird
the sea is a body of water

explanation.surface: A town scene with a bird floating on the water.
explanation.walkthrough: Swansea is a coastal city in south Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Swansea is a Welsh port, so it is an example of an urban settlement.

clue.text: Moves up since first of challenges is over

parts.note: as can mean since, as in 'as it was raining'

indicators.note: first of asks for only the opening letter of the following word

parts.note: the opening letter of challenges
something that is over ends

explanation.surface: Someone climbs a ranking because the initial round of contests has finished.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascend is to climb or rise, so the verb in the third person matches moves up.

clue.text: The way to get a six-pack? It's in drinks

definitions.text: The way to get a six-pack?

indicators.note: in says one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: to sup is to drink
taken as written

explanation.surface: A beer drinker's joke that the route to a six-pack is through drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Six-pack' suggests cans of beer, but it means toned stomach muscles; drinks is a verb here, as in sips.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing these abdominal exercises builds the visible stomach muscles that people call a six-pack.

clue.text: Again, come out for self-styled VIP

indicators.note: come out suggests the letters break loose from their order and regroup

parts.note: the fodder, used letter for letter

explanation.surface: A self-important celebrity is invited to make another appearance.
explanation.definitionFit: An egomaniac is obsessed with their own importance, someone who regards themselves as a very important person.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: piped and baked mashed potato, an elegant side dish
second meaning: the noblewoman addressed with this formal title

explanation.walkthrough: It sounds like a servant offering potatoes to a noble. Duchess potatoes are mashed potato piped into swirls and baked.
explanation.definitionFit: The name covers a dish of piped potato and the wife of a duke, who is addressed formally with that honorific.

clue.text: Can Simon Armitage drive with this?

definitions.text: Can Simon Armitage drive with this?

parts.words: Can Simon Armitage drive with this?
parts.note: surface reading: asking whether a particular man holds the document that lets him drive a car
setter's reading: Armitage is the UK Poet Laureate, so the permit is the freedom writers take with the rules of language

explanation.surface: Wondering if a famous writer is legally allowed behind the wheel.
explanation.walkthrough: Simon Armitage is Britain's Poet Laureate; a licence in British spelling is the noun for a permit.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means the freedom a writer takes to bend grammar or facts for artistic effect, punning on a driving permit.

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters lying inside the next word

parts.note: the letters sit in the middle of tragedy

explanation.surface: An old and respected figure plays a role in a tragic drama.
explanation.definitionFit: Venerable describes someone respected because of great age, so it overlaps with being old.

clue.text: Caress most of bottom frequently to begin with (one's amenable)

definitions.note: the answer names a person who is amenable; the definition is a clause describing them

indicators.note: most of means drop the final letter of the following word
to begin with places the following pieces before the word for caress

parts.note: ass is an informal word for the backside
oft is an old word for often
to caress is to touch gently

explanation.surface: A cheeky line suggesting that whoever keeps getting their behind stroked is an obliging sort.
explanation.walkthrough: ASS loses its last letter to give AS; AS and OFT come first, then TOUCH, making A SOFT TOUCH.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft touch is someone easily persuaded or taken advantage of, which is an idiom for a pliable, obliging person.

clue.text: We part at revolting Adam's Ale

indicators.note: revolting means rising up and overturning order, so the letters are thrown into a new arrangement

parts.note: the fodder, used letter for letter

explanation.surface: Someone splits from a partner over a disgusting drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Adam's Ale is an old jocular name for plain water, since the first man had nothing else to drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Adam's Ale is a humorous idiom for drinking water, and the kitchen supply is the everyday example.

indicators.note: carrying means holding something within, so the country wraps around the paper

parts.note: a country in Europe
a rag is a disparaging word for a newspaper

explanation.surface: A nation delivering a bunch of flowers wrapped in newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: Rag is a dismissive term for a low-quality newspaper; bouquet here means a smell rather than flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: Bouquet is used of the pleasant smell of wine or flowers, so it is a synonym for scent.

parts.note: Gene Wilder was the American comic actor of Willy Wonka fame
a rally is a motor race over public roads

explanation.surface: Remarking that, on the whole, the contest became more frantic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wilder' looks like the comparative of wild, but it is the actor's surname.
explanation.definitionFit: By and large is an idiom meaning on the whole, in most cases, as a rule.

parts.note: the Douglas fir is a well-known conifer
St is the standard abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: It reads like a postal address: house number one on Douglas Street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No 1' looks like a house number in the address, but it is the definition; Douglas only stands for the tree that takes its name.
explanation.definitionFit: Number one is the item in top position, so first is its ordinal equivalent.

clue.text: Reportedly I spill the beans on the cake?

definitions.note: the answer is the thing found on the cake

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is heard said, so the words are taken by their sound

parts.note: to spill the beans is to sing, slang for confessing to the police

explanation.surface: A confession that sounds like a criminal's, ending with a nod to the phrase 'icing on the cake'.
explanation.definitionFit: Icing is the sugary coating spread over a cake, the topping that sits there.

clue.text: Designer admits fashion finally is sound

indicators.note: admits means lets inside, so the designer's name holds the selected letter

parts.note: Coco Chanel, the French fashion designer

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word before it

parts.note: the closing letter of fashion

explanation.surface: A couturier concedes that their latest style is solid and sensible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like an adjective meaning reliable, but it is a noun: a narrow stretch of sea. N goes inside CHANEL: CHAN-N-EL.
explanation.definitionFit: A sound is a narrow sea passage between two landmasses, and a channel is the same geographical feature.

indicators.note: rubbish describes something badly made, so the letters of the following word are muddled

parts.note: the dash is read as the minus sign
the letters of clue rearranged

explanation.surface: A solver's cry of delight, then a grumble that the clue is no good.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash in the clue is punctuation on the surface but a minus sign in the wordplay. Wee is Scots for small, not a cry of joy.
explanation.definitionFit: Wee is a Scottish and informal word for tiny, and minuscule means extremely small.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: of meat or fish, not preserved by smoking or salting
second meaning: not yet healed of an illness

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a lifelong non-smoker who is ill anyway; smoked refers to preserving meat, not cigarettes.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes unpreserved ham or bacon, and also a patient whose illness has not been healed.

indicators.note: madness implies a crazed jumble, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the answer to 12 across
taken as written

explanation.surface: Older people with a crazy streak are put in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Captains head teams or ships, so they are people in command of a group.

indicators.note: to inject is to put something inside, so the drug goes into the nurse

parts.note: a carer looks after someone who is ill
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Phoning a nurse so that they can give an injection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Calling' looks like phoning, but it is a noun meaning vocation. E goes inside CARER: CAR-E-ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A calling is a vocation, the line of work a person follows through life.

clue.text: Andrew and I get on — it's a match!

taken as written
to get on is to grow older

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled that they and Andrew hit it off, declaring a perfect pairing.
explanation.walkthrough: MARR comes from Andrew Marr, the BBC political interviewer.
explanation.definitionFit: A match can mean a wedding or a union between two people, so it serves as a synonym for wedlock.

taken as written

clue.text: Scruffy Uncle Fin, with hesitation, is a trendsetter

explanation.definitionFit: An influencer is a person, typically on social media, whose taste and endorsements shape what others buy and wear.

clue.text: Trio not right for you once

indicators.note: not right means leave out the letter that abbreviates right

parts.note: a trio is a group of three

explanation.surface: A three-piece group that is not suitable for you in times past.
explanation.walkthrough: R stands for right; removing it from THREE leaves THEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Thee is the archaic object form of thou, the old singular pronoun used for addressing one person.

films are thin coatings or layers

explanation.walkthrough: 'Films' suggests cinema, but here it means thin coatings.
explanation.definitionFit: A team is made up of the people who take part in a game, its squad of sportsmen.

definitions.note: the clue at 16 across reads 'No 1, Douglas Street?', which is one of these
